maya: Quick heads-up — seeing a regression in multi-GPU inference when KV cache is enabled after the recent kernel-selector change. ~3-4% token throughput drop on 8xA100, p99 latency slightly up. Not huge but consistent across runs.

sanjay: Which commit / selector change? and which model+seq len?

maya: selector: runtime@3.14.0 -> runtime@3.15.0 (kernel pick logic changed to prefer cuBLASLt for small matmuls). Model: redwood-open-13b-ql8, seq_len ~512 typical, batching heuristics bumped to default-batch=8.

liam: perf-bot ran a quick profile on the failing run, pasting top lines: 

perf-bot: ```
step  : 0.0012s compute, 0.0009s all-reduce, 0.0006s kv-restore, 0.0007s kernel-selection
step  : all-reduce wait up +20% vs baseline
hot   : gemm_small_k (cuBLASLt)  28%
hot   : kv-restore-serialize    16%
hot   : rpc/serialize           8%
```

alex: Interesting. My guess: cuBLASLt kernel has higher launch/setup overhead for many small matmuls we do during KV apply, so we lose comm/compute overlap. Also KV sharding layout might be forcing an extra cross-device gather before local kernel run. Have we profiled comm timeline (NCCL/UCX) vs compute?

maya: I captured NCCL traces — timeline shows more barrier-like stalls around the KV apply phase. Looks like an extra all-reduce/all-gather pair that wasn't there before. Could be due to shard mapping + pipeline/tensor parallel staging order.

sanjay: Remind me the current KV shard mapping rules? I thought we shard KV by tensor-parallel slice (TP) and replicate across PP stages. If PP reordering changed, could be mismatched expectation and triggers fallback gather.

alex: Current: shard_policy = "tp_primary_then_replicate" (i.e., split heads across TP ranks, replicate per PP stage). That minimizes memory but requires synchronized gather when PP stage boundary needs full KV for attention. For interleaved PP schedules we might be paying the gather cost at an unfortunate time.

liam: TL;DR hypothesis: kernel choice -> slower per-layer local compute -> reduces overlap window so the all-reduce cost is less hidden. Combined with a PP boundary gather introduced by shard policy results in net perf regression.

maya: Proposed quick experiments: 
- run with forced kernel=legacy-cublas for small gemms (to see delta)
- try kv.shard_policy = "replicate_hot_layers" (replicate top N layers of KV across TP ranks to avoid gather)
- run with different batch sizes (4,8,16) to see batching heuristics interaction

sanjay: I can patch a runtime toggle to force legacy kernels and a toggle for shard_policy. I'll also add a per-step trace that logs when KV gather happens (one-line marker).

maya: Command I'll run: 
```bash
./run_infer.sh --model redwood-open-13b-ql8 --gpus 8 
  --runtime-flag kernel_selector=force_legacy 
  --kv-config shard_policy=replicate_hot_layers:2 
  --batch 8 
  --trace kv_gather_marker=1 
```

liam: If you can dump per-step NCCL timing (allreduce/allgather start/end) that helps. I'll add a quick script to correlate kernel launch times with NCCL waits.

maya: Ran the forced-legacy kernel + replicate_hot_layers:2 test (single run): 
- baseline (new selector + tp_shard): throughput 100 tokens/s
- forced-legacy + replicate_hot_layers:2: throughput 106 tokens/s
- forced-legacy only: 103 tokens/s
- replicate_hot_layers:2 only: 104 tokens/s
So both changes help; combined gives best result. Preliminary but consistent across 3 runs.

alex: Nice signal. That supports both hypotheses (kernel overhead + shard-induced gather). For rollout: we can either revert selector change for small matmuls or add a microkernel path for small matmuls that avoids launch overhead. For KV sharding, consider adaptive shard_policy: replicate hot layers if PP count>1 and interleaving=true.

sanjay: Action items: 
1) I’ll add a perf regression test that runs KV-heavy workload on 8xA100 nightly and compares throughput p95.
2) Add runtime knob to auto-replicate top-K layers based on observed gather frequency.
3) Track a kernel-selector flag to prefer legacy for small <XxY matmuls until we have a fused microkernel.

maya: I'll paste the reproducible run logs + perf traces to the datadog folder and open a small PR with the commands used. Link: https://gist.github.com/redwood/perf-kv-2119 (logs + traces).

liam: I'll try a microkernel prototype that fuses the KV apply + small gemm to avoid launch overhead and see if it restores overlap. ETA tomorrow.

alex: Great. Marking this P0 for the next perf triage. Thanks for the quick hunting everyone. :thumbsup:

maya: Cool — will update thread with the PR + baseline numbers when I have 10 run median.

perf-bot: nightly-kv-regression-check scheduled (will post results in #eng-runtime).
